Cardiff 1-0 Birmingham: Yousef Salech steers Bluebirds to victory
Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Cardiff City and Birmingham City at the Cardiff City Stadium on Saturday; Yousef Salech misses penalty but then scores winner.
Saturday 24 October 2026 19:08, UK
Cardiff halted Birmingham's winning run as Yousef Salech secured a 1-0 victory to continue the Bluebirds' climb up the Championship.
Salech was named among the home substitutes initially, but defender Krystian Bielik suffered an injury in the warm-up and had to drop out on an afternoon of relentless rain in the Welsh capital.
The late change saw Cardiff reshuffle their resources and Salech plunder a first-half winner, his sixth goal of the season coming 10 minutes after James Beadle had saved his spot-kick.
Cardiff have now recorded three straight home wins as they continue to show real signs of adapting to life in the second tier following promotion from League One.
Birmingham had arrived on the back of three successive wins without conceding, and remain in the play-off places after suffering their first defeat since September 9.
Cardiff manager Brian Barry-Murphy was serving a touchline ban after receiving his third yellow card of the season.
Both sets of players wore black armbands to mark the 60th anniversary of the Aberfan disaster, in which 116 children were among the 144 who died in the Welsh mining village, and a minute's silence before kick-off was impeccably observed.
Salech featured for the first time in five weeks after a shoulder injury, but could not pull down a Joel Bagan pass that would have taken him through on goal.
Luis Vazquez's wait for a first Birmingham goal went on as the Argentinian striker was unable to connect with Jay Stansfield's cross.
Cardiff were awarded a spot-kick after 21 minutes when Tomoki Iwata dragged down Perry Ng at a corner. Salech sent the penalty low to Beadle's right, but the effort lacked power and the Birmingham goalkeeper pushed the ball to safety.
It was the second successive spot-kick Cardiff had missed following Chris Willock's failure to convert against Watford.
But Salech quickly made amends by holding off Phil Neumann from Ollie Tanner's cross and producing a tidy turn and finish past Beadle.
Some Birmingham players held their arms aloft believing Neumann had been sent to the floor by a foul, but referee Tim Robinson clearly saw it as a case of Salech being stronger.
Beadle came to Birmingham's rescue at the start of the second half, denying Cian Ashford with his legs after Tanner and Salech had opened up the visitors.
Salech fired just past the base of a post as Cardiff increased intensity in the search for a second goal and Beadle fielded Ashford's attempt from distance.
Birmingham had not tested Nathan Trott until Stansfield met Alex Cochrane's cross, but it was a routine stop to say the least and Cardiff were untroubled until the closing stages.
Marvin Ducksch headed Max Bird's cross wide and Birmingham's best chance came two minutes from time when Trott superbly kept out Demarai Gray from point-blank range.

The managers
Cardiff head coach Brian Barry-Murphy:
"We understood what the day meant to everybody, so to get the victory that was so badly wanted is very special for everyone. It was very important for the players to watch the footage we saw, and to understand what the people there have been through.
"I think we're at our best when we're playing a very intense type of football.
"Sometimes we're good enough to win and sometimes we're not, but that's what we're always striving for, to play that type of aggressive, front-footed performance."
Birmingham manager Chris Davies:
"The best team won, in any game if you're second to the ball that much it's always going to be hard.
"Every time we had possession of the ball there was a blue shirt on us. They are a side who do put the press on and we just couldn't get close to their box.
"We were very disorganised for the goal, how easy it came in to the box and the goal. That's unlike us. We gave ourselves a big job to recover from that and we expected more."

קארדיף סיטי עצרה את רצף הניצחונות של בירמינגהאם סיטי לאחר שגברה עליה 0-2 באצטדיון הבית שלה במסגרת הצ'מפיונשיפ. החלוץ יוסוף סאלח, שפתח בספסל ונכנס עקב פציעה בחימום, כבש את שער הניצחון בדקה הראשונה של המשחק מבישול של אולי טאנר, זאת לאחר שהחמץ בעיטת עונשין מנקודת הפנדל עשר דקות קודם לכן.

הניצחון מעלה את קארדיף במעלה הטבלה ומאשר את התאקלמותה בליגה השנייה לאחר ההעפלה מליגה אחת. שחקני שתי הקבוצות ענדו סרטים שחורים לציון יום השנה האסון באברפן, ודקת דומייה נשמרה לפני שריקת הפתיחה לזכר הקורבנות.
